claim: git checkout --no-overlay <C> -- <pathspecs> (a) updates pathspec-matched files changed in <C>, (b) DELETES pathspec-matched files that are absent from <C> — deletion propagation is the load-bearing behavior the Wave-3 Apply executor's working-tree realization step depends on — and (c) behaves identically across the supported git version range.
load_bearing_behavior: deletion propagation: a working-tree file matched by the pathspec but absent from <C>'s tree is removed from BOTH the working tree and the index, making them match <C> exactly for the approved paths

observed.how: spike/no-overlay-repro.test.mjs builds a fixture repo (commit A holds f1..f4; commit C modifies f1 and f4 and removes f2; working tree reset to A so it holds both pathspec files), runs `git checkout --no-overlay <C> -- f1.txt f2.txt`, and asserts: f1 updated to C's content, f2 deleted from working tree AND index, f3/f4 untouched (pathspec scoping — f4 differs in C but is outside the pathspec), and re-running converges to the same state (idempotency, required for journaled retry).
observed.verification_discipline: the repro runs on the gate runner's installed git on EVERY `node --test` run and FAILS the suite if measurement ever contradicts this verdict — the stamp cannot silently rot; the runner's git version is asserted >= the supported floor

supported_git_range.basis: --no-overlay and checkout.overlayMode were introduced in git 2.22; the documented no-overlay semantics ('files that appear in the index and working tree, but not in <tree-ish> are removed, to make them match <tree-ish> exactly') have been stable through current releases
supported_git_range.single_version_honesty: only the gate runner's installed git version is OBSERVED by the repro; the claim across the rest of the range is DOCUMENTED (git release notes / man page), not observed. Mitigation carried into the executor design: the Wave-3 Apply executor MUST assert `git version >= 2.22` at runtime before using --no-overlay, and this repro re-verifies real behavior on every suite run on whatever git the host has, so a behavioral regression in a future git surfaces as a red gate, not a silent executor corruption.

refuted_fallback_spec.status: pre-specified, DORMANT — activates ONLY if the repro ever measures REFUTED (per the frozen plan: the executor is neither built on an unverified claim nor redesigned to appease an unverified objection)
refuted_fallback_spec.realization:
per-path journaled realization under the SAME Apply journal, replacing the single --no-overlay call in the executor's step 5 while every other step (lock, revalidation vs S, temp-index compile, one commit via commit-tree, compare-and-swap update-ref) is unchanged: for each approved path p in the plan — if p exists in 's tree, run `git -C checkout --

` (checkout-for-content: updates index + working tree for p); if p is absent from 's tree, delete the working-tree file at p, then reconcile the index entry with `git -C update-index --force-remove --

` (delete-for-deletion).
refuted_fallback_spec.invariants: each per-path step is journaled as {path, op, state} before execution and marked done after; the whole realization is idempotent (a missing file / already-absent index entry counts as done) and is retried from the journal on interruption; the commit and ref are already durable before realization begins, so no interruption can lose content — identical durability semantics to the CONFIRMED branch
